test_title: PYST 45: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held on 9 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The mother-in-law deliberately __rained on the new bride’s parade__ when she asked her to change the dress of her choice.

options.text: Make someone tearful out of viciousness

solution:
The correct option is **"To spoil a moment"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given underlined word is an **idiom**. 
 
• The meaning of **rain on** the new bride's parade is spoiling someone's pleasure.
 
• The given sentence indicates that the **mother-in-law** spoiled the new bride's pleasure intentionally.
 
• The third option is **"To spoil a moment"** which means a moment is to be spoiled. That meaning is related to the underlined **idiom**.

The **correct sentence** is The mother-in-law deliberately **spoiled the new bride’s moment__** when she asked her to change the dress of her choice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **"Force upon"** means "to make someone to do something using threats or force".
 
• The second option refers to make someone cry through **viciousness**.
 
• If we save someone from his or her **embarrassing moment**, we can use the last idiom which is in the option.
 
• The above three phrases do not match the underlined phrase.
